docs.title: AI traceability for CNP: legal map (EU/France) and VictoriaStack implementation
docs.text:
Research date: 2026-11-13. This is a factual map, not legal advice. Convention: "LAW SAYS" = binding text. "GUIDANCE" = non-binding official text. "BEST PRACTICE" = my synthesis or practitioner advice. Confidence: [HIGH] primary source read this session. [MED] secondary source or primary source only partly read. [LOW] inferred or unverified. Stale flag: anything older than 12 months (before 2025-11-13) is marked [STALE - date].

Access caveat: eur-lex.europa.eu pages do not render through my fetcher (JS-only). For AI Act article text I used the European Commission "AI Act Service Desk" article pages, which state they follow the EUR-Lex consolidated version of 2026-07-27 and flag Omnibus changes with NEW/AMENDED markers. The EUR-Lex consolidated text exists at CELEX 02024R1689-20260727 (seen in search results, not rendered). Treat EUR-Lex as the binding source and re-check anything load-bearing there.

docs.title: A1. EU AI Act (Reg. 2024/1689) as amended by the Digital Omnibus on AI
docs.text:
Omnibus status in Nov 2026: adopted, in force, high-risk postponed. [HIGH on dates/content, MED on OJ publication day] - Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, dated 2026-07-08, amends Reg. 2024/1689, 2018/1139 and 2023/1230. ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744/oj. Search result metadata from eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744 confirms title and date. Publication in the OJ on 2026-07-24 and entry into force 2026-07-27 come from law-firm sources [MED]. - Political deal 2026-05-07, Parliament vote 2026-06-16, Council adoption 2026-06-29 (secondary sources) [MED]. - Dates per the Commission's AI Act Service Desk timeline (accessed 2026-11-13) [HIGH]:

Date What applies Changed by Omnibus 2025-02-02 Chapters I-II: definitions, Art. 4 AI literacy, Art. 5 prohibitions No 2025-08-02 GPAI provider obligations (Art. 53-55), governance, national authorities and penalties No 2026-08-02 Most rules incl. Art. 50 transparency, Commission enforcement powers on GPAI No 2026-12-02 New Art. 5 prohibitions (non-consensual intimate deepfakes, CSAM). Transition for Art. 50(2) marking for generative systems already on the market before 2026-08-02 (Art. 111(4)) Yes 2027-08-02 Sandboxes; legacy GPAI models placed before 2025-08-02 must comply Sandbox date yes 2027-12-02 High-risk Annex III (Art. 6(2)) rules Yes (was 2026-08-02) 2028-08-02 High-risk Annex I products (Art. 6(1)) Yes (was 2027-08-02)

Sources: https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act and https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/ai-act-explorer/digital-omnibus/ (the latter is an unofficial but text-verified tracker) [HIGH/MED]. - Art. 4 AI literacy was rewritten: providers and deployers "shall take measures to support the development of AI literacy", no specific individual level required (Service Desk page, all 3 paragraphs marked AMENDED). Still in force since 2025-02-02. [HIGH] - Art. 12, 19, 21, 26, 72(1) text is NOT amended by the Omnibus (no AMENDED markers on the Service Desk pages; Omnibus summary page says Arts. 12/19/26 are untouched). [HIGH] - Art. 25 was amended (value chain). Art. 27 FRIA may reuse a GDPR DPIA. [HIGH] - Art. 72: Service Desk page says the Commission template/guidance for the post-market monitoring plan is due by 2027-09-02. Not cross-checked on EUR-Lex. [MED] - Not found: whether the 2027-12-02 date can slip again. Annex III content itself unchanged on the page I read.

Article-by-article (LAW SAYS)

Article What it says Applies to URL Art. 12(1)-(2) High-risk systems must technically allow automatic recording of events (logs) over the system lifetime, at a level enabling traceability for: (a) identifying risk situations or substantial modification, (b) post-market monitoring (Art. 72), © monitoring of operation by deployers (Art. 26(5)). Art. 12(3) lists minimum fields only for remote biometric identification: start/end time of each use, reference database, input data that led to a match, identity of persons verifying results. Provider design duty, high-risk only https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-12 Art. 19 Providers keep Art. 12(1) logs under their control for a period appropriate to the intended purpose, at least 6 months, "without prejudice to applicable Union or national law" (data protection law named). High-risk providers https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-19 Art. 21(2) On reasoned request, provider gives the competent authority access to Art. 12(1) logs under its control. Confidentiality per Art. 78. High-risk providers https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-21 Art. 26(1)-(2) Deployer uses system per instructions; assigns human oversight to persons with competence, training, authority, support. High-risk deployers https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-26 Art. 26(5) Deployer monitors operation on basis of instructions for use; if risk, informs provider/distributor and market surveillance authority without undue delay and suspends use; serious incidents reported to provider first, then importer/distributor and authorities. High-risk deployers same Art. 26(6) Deployer keeps automatically generated logs under its control at least 6 months, unless other Union/national law (esp. data protection) provides otherwise. High-risk deployers same Art. 26(7) Employer-deployers inform workers' representatives and affected workers before using a high-risk system at work. High-risk deployers same Art. 26(11) Deployers of Annex III systems that decide or assist decisions on natural persons inform them they are subject to a high-risk system. High-risk deployers same Art. 50(1) Providers design systems that interact directly with natural persons so people are informed they interact with AI, unless obvious to a reasonably well-informed person. Any AI system provider, in force since 2026-08-02 https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-50 Art. 50(2) Providers of systems (including GPAI systems) generating synthetic audio, image, video or text mark outputs in machine-readable, detectable format. Exempt: assistive function for standard editing or no substantial alteration of input. Transition to 2026-12-02 for systems on market before 2026-08-02. Providers of generative systems same Art. 50(4) Deployers disclose deepfakes and AI text published to inform the public on matters of public interest, unless human review and editorial responsibility. Deployers publishing content same Art. 53, 55 GPAI model providers: technical documentation, downstream information (53(1)(b)), copyright policy, training-data summary; systemic-risk models add evaluation, incident reporting to AI Office (55(1)©). GPAI model providers (Anthropic, Google, Meta, Mistral...), not downstream deployers n/a Art. 72 Providers of high-risk systems run documented post-market monitoring collecting performance data over lifetime (deployers' data included). High-risk providers https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-72 Art. 73 Providers of high-risk systems report serious incidents to market surveillance authority of the Member State: general case at most 15 days after awareness; widespread infringement or Art. 3(49)(b) at most 2 days; death at most 10 days; incomplete initial report allowed. High-risk providers https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-73 Art. 25 A deployer or third party becomes provider of a high-risk system if it rebrands it, substantially modifies it, or changes the intended purpose (including of a GPAI system) so that it becomes high-risk. 25(4): written agreement between high-risk provider and third-party suppliers of tools/models/components, FOSS tools excluded, GPAI models not covered by that exemption. Tenant app builders and the platform as supplier https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-25 Art. 3(3), 3(4), 3(11) Provider includes whoever develops a system and puts it into service under its own name, "putting into service" includes in-house first use. Deployer uses a system under its authority. Role qualification https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-3

All rows [HIGH] except where noted, with the caveat that the service desk summaries paraphrase; verbatim text is on EUR-Lex.

What applies to CNP today (my reading, not legal advice) [LOW to MED, role qualification is a legal judgment] - LAW SAYS: the AI Act has no general logging duty for non-high-risk systems. Art. 12/19/26(6)/72/73 are scoped to high-risk systems, which apply from 2027-12-02 at the earliest for Annex III. - CNP as a platform deploying Claude/Gemini/Ollama models: the model providers carry Art. 53/55. CNP becomes a GPAI model provider only if it substantially modifies a model. The Commission guidelines (2025-07-18, secondary summaries) use a one-third-of-original-training-compute test. Primary text not read in full. [MED] - CNP-built assistants and hosted agents (portal MCP server, kagent agents): CNP is probably the "provider" of those AI systems, since in-house putting into service counts (Art. 3(3), 3(11)). They are most likely not high-risk. Duties then: Art. 4 (support literacy), Art. 5 (prohibitions), Art. 50(1) disclosure unless obvious, possibly Art. 50(2) marking of generated text if the exemption for assistive editing does not fit. Whether Art. 50(2) bites on internal dev agents is an open reading. [LOW] - Tenant app in Annex III (4(a) recruiting/CV screening, 4(b) performance monitoring, 3(a)-(d) education admission/grading/proctoring): the tenant is provider or deployer and carries Art. 12/19/26/72/73. CNP is at most a supplier under Art. 25(4) and gets a contractual duty to give information and technical access. Annex III list: https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-3 [HIGH]. Art. 6(3) derogation not checked. - Enforcement authority in France: designation still unsettled. A DGE/DGCCRF scheme was published Sept 2025, a Senate vote on the DDADUE bill on 2026-02-18 was reported, final adoption not found. Sources conflict on CNIL's role. [LOW]. https://www.entreprises.gouv.fr/priorites-et-actions/transition-numerique/soutenir-le-developpement-de-lia-au-service-de-0

Harmonised standards and logging [MED] - CEN-CENELEC JTC 21 is working on 10 Commission-requested areas, including record keeping, human oversight, transparency, cybersecurity. Source: https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/ai-act-standardisation [HIGH]. - The first one to reach the OJ is EN 18286 (quality management, Art. 17), via Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2274, per the same Commission page. Not about logging. [HIGH on Commission page; the 2026-10-14 OJ date is from a secondary source] - prEN ISO/IEC 24970 "AI system logging": ISO/IEC SC 42 DIS 24970:2025 adopted as CEN draft. CEN public enquiry 2025-11-28 to 2026-01-25 (Lithuanian tracker). DIN lists a follow-on FprEN ISO/IEC 24970:2026 under CEN/CLC/JTC 21/WG 3. ISO page shows "Under publication". I could not confirm final publication nor whether it is cited in the OJ as a harmonised standard. [MED]. Sources: https://standards.iteh.ai/catalog/standards/cen/38472bd6-ab5c-4908-ac64-6990f45027e6/pren-iso-iec-24970 , https://www.iso.org/standard/88723.html (403 to my fetcher, status taken from search snippet). - ISO/IEC 42001:2023 Annex A control A.6.2.8 (AI system recording of event logs): organisation decides in which lifecycle phases logging is enabled, minimum when in use. Control text is paywalled, wording from vendor sites. Claims of mandatory integrity or immutability are vendor additions. [MED/LOW] - Practical consequence: no harmonised logging standard gives presumption of conformity yet. Anything built now is a reasonable design, not a presumption of conformity.

docs.title: A2. GDPR and CNIL
docs.text:
LAW SAYS (GDPR, Reg. 2016/679; ELI https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj, not re-fetched this session, article numbers from standard knowledge) [MED] - Art. 5(1)© minimisation, 5(1)(e) storage limitation, 5(1)(f) integrity and confidentiality, 5(2) accountability, Art. 25 by design, Art. 32 security, Art. 30 register, Art. 35 DPIA, Art. 15 access, Art. 22 automated decisions, Art. 33-34 breach notification (72 h to supervisory authority). - Prompts and agent traces routinely contain personal data (names, emails, code with data, tickets). So prompt/response logs are personal data processing with CNP or the tenant as controller. A controller needs a purpose and a legal basis for the log processing itself.

CNIL logging recommendation: deliberation no. 2021-122 of 2021-10-14 [HIGH, read in full] [STALE - 2021-10-14, still the reference] PDF: https://www.cnil.fr/sites/cnil/files/atoms/files/recommandation_-_journalisation.pdf . Legifrance JORFTEXT000044272396. - Scope: application logs, not perimeter logs (para. 2). Non-prescriptive (para. 1). - Para. 6: record creation, consultation, modification, deletion with individually identified author, timestamp, nature of operation, reference of the data concerned. "Avoid duplicating the processed data within the logs." - Para. 7: store segregated from the main system, write-only for the applications, no overwrite; access rights to logs based on strict necessity. - Para. 8: retain 6 months to 1 year. Para. 9: purpose is mainly active security (alerts, detection), formalise alert processing. Para. 10: ex post breach investigation. - Para. 11: reuse for another purpose may be a purpose diversion; use a usage charter or alert on modification access. - Para. 12: minimise personal data in logs; ensure confidentiality, availability, integrity; recommends to timestamp and sign logs at creation. - Para. 13: inform authorised users of logging, data and duration. Data subject rights on logs are exercised with the controller of the main processing. - Paras. 16-17: more than one year can be justified for internal control if risk of misuse is demonstrated (sensitive data at scale, systematic surveillance) and documented investigation procedures exist. - Para. 18: do not collect sensitive or highly personal data in logs that is not already in the processing.

CNIL AI recommendations [MED, STALE for 2024-2025 fiches] - Fiches IA (2024-04 to 2025-07) cover development of AI systems: legal basis, DPIA, security, rights, annotation, model status. No fiche on logs, none dedicated to deployment. List: https://www.cnil.fr/fr/les-fiches-pratiques-ia . [HIGH] [STALE - 2025-07] - Rights over prompts: CNIL states GDPR applies to use of models through prompts, and rights requests should say whether they target training data or the model. https://www.cnil.fr/fr/ia-respecter-lexercice-des-droits-des-personnes [MED, STALE] - EDPB Opinion 28/2024 (2024-12-17): models are not automatically anonymous, legitimate interest needs a three-step test. [MED, STALE - 2024-12-17] - CNIL/CIANum note "IA agentique et protection des donnees personnelles", July 2026 [HIGH, read]. https://www.cnil.fr/sites/default/files/2026-07/ia-cianum-cnil.pdf . This is an analysis note, not a formal CNIL deliberation, and says the AI Act (full application 2027) has no specific agent rules. It proposes: - Traceability so that for each task the user can identify personal data used, agents involved, third-party services called, exchanges and their chronology. This also builds a chain of responsibility. - Data minimisation and purpose limitation per task, user control over accessible data. - Art. 22 GDPR remains fully applicable. CJEU SCHUFA ruling: human intervention must be meaningful. - Memory partitioned per agent, expiry or size limits, one session per processing. - Sandboxing, human validation for critical actions classified by risk (data access, modification, deletion, outbound data), kill switch, filtering of inputs/outputs, evaluation. - Notes that joint EDPB/Commission guidelines on AI Act and GDPR interplay are expected by end 2026 (not found published). [LOW] - ANSSI "Les essentiels: Securiser un systeme IA agentique" v1.0, October 2026 [HIGH, read]. https://messervices.cyber.gouv.fr/documents-guides/anssi_essentiels_ia_agentique_1.0.pdf . Seven principles. Directly relevant items: - Classify agent actions as autonomous, mandatory human approval, or forbidden. Human approval for critical actions, sensitive data access, identity or rights changes, production deployments. Keep the approval mechanism out of the agent's reach. Show the approver the exact action, purpose, expected effects. Execute only the approved action. - Deterministic authorisation independent of the agent, default deny. - Keep secrets out of model context, memory and logs. - Keep agent logs out of reach of agent modification, so the full sequence "request, authorisation, action, result" can be reconstructed after an incident. - Monitor in production against the documented mission (UEBA), emergency stop with access revocation, per-tenant and per-environment memory. - Cites the AI Act Art. 6 for high-risk systems. - ANSSI "Recommandations de securite pour un systeme d'IA generative" ANSSI-PA-102, 2024-04-29 [STALE - 2024-04-29]: R9, no automatic execution of critical IS actions. [MED, from search snippet]

Tension "log everything" vs "minimise" and how it resolves [BEST PRACTICE] - The AI Act has no logging duty for CNP today, and for high-risk the 6-month floor in Art. 19/26(6) is explicitly subject to data protection law. So the legal floor for content logging is zero for CNP, and the GDPR sets a ceiling by purpose. - Pattern: always log metadata and decisions (who, what, when, model, tokens, tool, approval, outcome, hashes), never content by default, content capture opt-in per project with a stated purpose, short retention for content, redaction at the gateway or collector, hash of content so integrity and non-repudiation hold without the text. - This matches the OTel spec default (content capture off) and CNIL para. 6, 12, 18.

docs.text: Instrument Status Nov 2026 Relevance to CNP NIS2 (Dir. 2022/2555) France transposition Not in force. Art. 23(4) timelines: early warning 24 h, notification 72 h, final report 1 month. [MED] Cyber Resilience Act (Reg. 2024/2847) Art. 14 reporting of actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents applies since 2026-09-11 via ENISA Single Reporting Platform. Remaining obligations from 2027-12-11. Sources: https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/cra-reporting plus law-firm notes [MED] Only for products with digital elements placed on the EU market by a manufacturer. An internal demo platform is likely out of scope. A tenant shipping a product is not. DORA (Reg. 2022/2554) Applies since 2025-01-17 Only if a client is a financial entity. docs.title: PART B. TECHNICAL STATE OF THE ART (Nov 2026)
B1. OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions
docs.text:
Status: all Development, not Stable. [HIGH] - GenAI and MCP conventions moved out of the main repo in semantic-conventions v1.42.0 (2026-06-12) to https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai . No tagged release, CHANGELOG has only "Unreleased", README gives no stability level, Schema URL "TODO". Latest commits seen: 2026-11-06 (#692, #513, #144), so it is moving daily. - Third-party posts claiming "stable" exist (one dated 2026-06-22). They conflict with the registry badges reported in dev.to (2026-07-16) and my reading of the repo. Treat "stable" claims as wrong. [MED] - Practical rule: pin the instrumentation versions and expect renames. Opt-in env for latest names: OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental (secondary sources, John Hodge post updated 2026-11-03 and Coralogix doc) [MED].

Content in the repo docs (docs/gen-ai/.md), read from raw.githubusercontent.com on 2026-11-13 [HIGH] - Spans: inference client spans (client-inference.md), embeddings, invoke_agent (INTERNAL for in-process agents, CLIENT variant for remote agent services, invoke_workflow when the app controls the flow), create_agent, execute_tool (INTERNAL, name execute_tool {gen_ai.tool.name}), retrieval, a2a, realtime. - Agent identity: gen_ai.agent.name, gen_ai.agent.id, gen_ai.agent.version, gen_ai.conversation.id (only when a real ID exists), gen_ai.main_agent resource entity. - Tool attributes: gen_ai.tool.name (required), gen_ai.tool.type, gen_ai.tool.call.id, and opt-in sensitive gen_ai.tool.call.arguments and gen_ai.tool.call.result. execute-tool.md defines NO approval, permission or user-confirmation attributes. Agent-as-tool adds gen_ai.transfer.mode and target. Skills add gen_ai.skill., process.executable.*, process.exit.code. - MCP (mcp.md): span name {mcp.method.name} {target}, attributes mcp.method.name, mcp.session.id, mcp.protocol.version, jsonrpc.request.id, error.type (tool_error when isError), context propagated in params._meta as unprefixed traceparent/tracestate/baggage. Metrics mcp.client|server.operation.duration and session.duration. MCP tool-call spans should merge into an existing execute_tool span when detectable. - Metrics (gen-ai-metrics.md): gen_ai.client.operation.duration, gen_ai.server.request.duration, gen_ai.server.time_per_output_token, gen_ai.server.time_to_first_token, gen_ai.invoke_agent.duration, .inference_calls, .tool_calls, gen_ai.execute_tool.duration. - Conflict on token metric name. The metrics page no longer lists gen_ai.client.token.usage. gen-ai-token-metrics.md defines counters gen_ai.client.inference.usage.input_tokens, .output_tokens, .cache_read.input_tokens, .cache_write.input_tokens, .reasoning.output_tokens and histograms gen_ai.client.inference.operation.input_tokens / output_tokens. Yet agentgateway (agentgateway_gen_ai_client_token_usage), the VictoriaMetrics/OpenLIT blog (gen_ai_client_token_usage_sum) and most SDKs still emit the older histogram. Expect both generations to coexist in your data for a while. Counters are the better base for cost sums. [HIGH on spec, HIGH on agentgateway docs] - Events: gen_ai.evaluation.result (gen_ai.evaluation.name, score.value, score.label, explanation, gen_ai.response.id), parented to the evaluated operation span when possible. Exception events gen_ai.invoke_agent.exception, gen_ai.execute_tool.exception (WARN severity). Inference-operation events are in client-inference.md (not read). - Content capture (gen-ai-spans.md): opt-in. Env var OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_CONTENT with NO_CONTENT (default), SPAN_ONLY, EVENT_ONLY, SPAN_AND_EVENT. Governs gen_ai.input.messages, gen_ai.output.messages, gen_ai.system_instructions, tool call args and results, retrieval queries, prompt variables, memory records. _ref variants (for example gen_ai.input.messages_ref) store a URI to external storage instead of inline content, which suits a "content in the Object Lock bucket, pointer in the trace" design. Docs warn the attributes "likely contain sensitive information including user/PII data". - Events vs span attributes: since v1.37.0 (2025-08) messages moved from per-message events to span attributes (secondary: John Hodge). The current spec lets you choose where content goes (span, event, both). Evaluation results are events. [MED] - Not found in spec: attributes for human approval, guardrail verdict, prompt-injection detection, user identity on GenAI spans. Use your own namespace (for example cnp.approval.*, cnp.guardrail.*) plus standard enduser.id and tenant attributes. This is a gap to document, not a standard to cite.

docs.title: B2. Who emits what
docs.text: Component What it emits Content capture Evidence agentgateway (Apache-2.0, 6.2k stars, pushed 2026-11-13; latest v1.7.0 2026-10-27) Traces via OTLP (policy-enabled, off by default on Kubernetes via AgentgatewayPolicy). Default span attrs: HTTP set, gen_ai.operation.name, provider.name, request.model, response.model, usage.input_tokens/output_tokens, agw.ai.original_model, mcp.method.name, mcp.target, mcp.session.id, mcp.resource., gen_ai.tool.name, mcp.error.; conditional jwt.sub, src.identity. Access logs per request with gen_ai.* fields and agw.ai.usage.cost.total, exportable as OTLP LogRecords. Prometheus: agentgateway_gen_ai_client_token_usage (labels token type, operation, system, request/response model, user_id when per-user API key rate limiting), agentgateway_cost_catalog_lookups_total. v1.7.0 adds cache, reasoning tokens, TTFT, session detection (x-claude-code-session-id), CEL MCP guardrails, guard scopes covering tool outputs by default. Guardrail verdicts and audit-mode detections go to metrics and the structured access log (not documented for traces). Prompt/completion logging not documented on the pages read. Tool calls opt-in via llm.toolCalls in access-log and tracing attributes (adds overhead). Guard audit mode still calls the provider (cost, latency) https://agentgateway.dev/docs/kubernetes/latest/documentation/llm/observability/ , https://agentgateway.dev/docs/standalone/latest/documentation/observability/traces/attribute-reference/ , https://agentgateway.dev/docs/kubernetes/main/documentation/llm/guardrails/overview/ , release v1.7.0 on GitHub [HIGH] kagent (Apache-2.0, 4.3k stars, v1.0.0 released 2026-11-09, v1.0.1 2026-11-12) v1.0.0 notes: OTEL via SDK-spec env vars, Weaver registry as telemetry contract, chat and execute_tool spans from runtimes, Python runtimes on upstream GenAI instrumentation, semconv metrics exported, legacy ADK spans dropped, trace context propagated on outbound LLM and MCP calls, harness invocation identity, trusted user as user.id, HITL pause on input-required. PR #1433 (merged 2026-03-10): controller tracing, A2A propagation, invoke_agent span with GenAI attributes. Docs page for 0.10.x showed span agent_run [agent] only and says 0.10.x is superseded by 1.0. v1.0.1 backport "honor runtime content capture settings" implies content capture is runtime-configurable. Exact setting not found https://api.github.com/repos/kagent-dev/kagent/releases , https://github.com/kagent-dev/kagent/pull/1433 [HIGH on release notes, docs for 1.0 tracing not found] MCP servers (yours) Only if instrumented. Spec defines mcp.* conventions and _meta propagation. Not researched per server SDK. opt-in args/results mcp.md [HIGH on spec] Ollama Not found: no native OTel. PRs open: #14203 (traces), #6537 (OTel metrics), #16998 (Prometheus metrics endpoint). None merged as of 2026-11-13. Third-party opentelemetry-instrumentation-ollama (OpenLLMetry) instruments the Python client only. n/a GitHub issues search 2026-11-13 [HIGH]. So measure local-model calls at agentgateway, not at Ollama. GPU metrics need a separate exporter [LOW, not verified] LiteLLM proxy OTel callback callbacks: ["otel"]; default is legacy span format, newer GenAI names behind OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental; behavior changed in v1.81.0 (litellm_request span collapsed by default). Enterprise-gated: key redaction in logs, audit logs, SSO. Licence boundary for OTel itself not confirmed. via callback config docs.litellm.ai, Coralogix, Fiddler pages [MED]. Not needed if agentgateway stays the gateway OpenLIT SDK Python/TS auto-instrumentation of 50+ libraries incl. MCP, emits GenAI attributes plus own cost extension (gen_ai.usage.cost). Evals scored through OpenLIT platform. Apache-2.0, 3.1k stars, pushed 2026-11-11. configurable https://victoriametrics.com/blog/victoriametrics-openlit-agents-observability/ (2026-07-03) [HIGH for the claims in that post] OpenLLMetry / Traceloop SDK Apache-2.0, 7.5k stars, pushed 2026-11-09. One secondary analysis says it still emits deprecated gen_ai.prompt/gen_ai.completion in places and adds traceloop.* attributes. Ownership claim (ServiceNow acquisition 2026-03) unverified. configurable futureagi.com, traceloop docs [LOW/MED] Claude Code and Claude Agent SDK CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1 plus OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER, OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER, OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER (+CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1 for traces, beta), standard OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_. Metrics: claude_code.token.usage, cost.usage, session.count, code_edit_tool.decision, active_time.total, lines_of_code, commit, pull_request counts. Log events: user_prompt, api_request (model, cost_usd, tokens, request_id), tool_result, tool_decision (decision plus source: config, hook, user_permanent, user_abort), api_error, mcp_server_connection, permission_mode_changed. Spans: claude_code.interaction > llm_request, tool (> tool.blocked_on_user, tool.execution), hook. W3C TRACEPARENT in and out, forwarded to Bash. Attributes: session.id, prompt.id, user.id (random local ID), user.email when authed. Agent SDK doc: inject enduser.id and tenant.id through OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES to get a per-user audit trail. Does NOT use gen_ai. names. Off by default. Opt-in: OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS, OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS, OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT (needs tracing), OTEL_LOG_ASSISTANT_RESPONSES, OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES (high sensitivity). Repo settings cannot enable telemetry, only managed settings https://code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage , https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/observability [HIGH]

docs.title: B3. Storage and query on the Victoria stack
docs.text:
State of the stack (from existing scratchpad file research-vm-ecosystem.md, same date, plus this session) [HIGH] - VictoriaTraces v0.13.0 (2026-11-05) is pre-GA, data structure not frozen. OTLP HTTP and gRPC ingest, Jaeger query API for Grafana, per-day partitions, default retention 7d, tenant by AccountID/ProjectID headers with vmauth for authorization. Docs page: https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriatraces/ - VictoriaLogs v1.54.0 (2026-11-13) GA since v1.0.0, OTLP logs at /insert/opentelemetry/v1/logs, no S3 storage, no per-stream or per-tenant retention. Use several instances with different retention for audit logs (30d content, 12m metadata, for example). vmalert supports rule type vlogs. - VictoriaMetrics: OTLP at /opentelemetry. -opentelemetry.usePrometheusNaming turns gen_ai.usage.cost into gen_ai_usage_cost_USD_sum (VM/OpenLIT blog). - Official reference pipeline: https://victoriametrics.com/blog/victoriametrics-openlit-agents-observability/ (2026-07-03) and companion repo https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/ai-observability (Apache-2.0, 9 commits, docker-compose with VM, VL, VT, Grafana, vmalert, rules/llm.yml, otelcol.yaml, one dashboard). Collector pattern: metrics pipeline strips high-cardinality labels (conversation, response and tool-call IDs, user.id); logs pipeline to VictoriaLogs with optional prompt capture; traces pipeline with tail sampling (keep errors, expensive runs, runs over 10 s, 5% of the rest). The post estimates 80 to 95% trace volume drop. OpenLIT's own destination doc lists the three OTLP endpoints (/opentelemetry, /insert/opentelemetry for logs and traces) and Grafana datasources: Prometheus type, VictoriaLogs plugin, Jaeger type. - Audit consequence of tail sampling: tail sampling is right for ops traces and wrong for the compliance record. Run two paths. Ops path sampled. Audit path unsampled but metadata-only, as log records.

Mapping of your needs [BEST PRACTICE unless marked] - GenAI dashboards: tokens, cost, latency, TTFT, errors from agentgateway Prometheus metrics and gen_ai.* metrics in VictoriaMetrics. Datasource prometheus type or victoriametrics-metrics-datasource. Traces via Jaeger datasource on VictoriaTraces, logs via victoriametrics-logs-datasource. - Cost per project, agent, user: agentgateway gives cost per request in logs and spans (agw.ai.usage.cost.total) and per-user token series when user_id label is on. A per-project label is not a default metric label. Add it as a custom access-log and span attribute through the policy CEL attributes (documented mechanism), then aggregate in LogsQL stats, and keep metrics labels bounded. Per-project label in metrics: not verified. Claude Code cost per user/team: claude_code.cost.usage with OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES team.id. - Tool-call audit trail: agentgateway MCP spans and access logs (mcp.method.name, gen_ai.tool.name, session id, jwt.sub) for gateway-routed calls. kagent execute_tool spans. Claude Code tool_decision and tool_result events. All carry trace IDs, so one LogsQL query by trace_id joins logs and spans. - Guardrail and prompt-injection events: agentgateway guardrail detections land in metrics and the access log. Alert with vmalert type vlogs on a verdict field. Exact field name not found, check a live log line. - Human-approval events: no OTel standard (confirmed absent in execute-tool.md). Emit one structured log record or span event per decision from CMP and the MCP server: cnp.approval.state (requested, confirmed, denied, cmp_pending, cmp_approved), cnp.approval.approver (Keycloak sub), cnp.action.hash (hash of exact action and parameters), cnp.approval.channel, trace context of the run. This mirrors the ANSSI principle of showing the exact action and executing only what was approved. - Evaluation scores: spec event gen_ai.evaluation.result, or metric gen_ai_evaluation_score as in the VM/OpenLIT blog. A nightly eval job writing these into VM is cheaper than a platform. - Per-run trace: propagate one traceparent from the CMP request, through MCP params._meta (spec), agentgateway, kagent (1.0 propagates on outbound LLM and MCP calls), sandbox processes (Claude Code forwards TRACEPARENT to Bash). Whether agentgateway extracts and continues an inbound traceparent: not verified in docs read, test it.

Tamper-evident audit trail options for a small stack [BEST PRACTICE, tools unevaluated] 1. S3 Object Lock in compliance mode (you already have it) as the system of record for the per-run "AI Act record", written at run end as a signed JSON object. This is WORM by storage guarantee. Matches CNIL para. 7 (write-only, segregated) and ANSSI principle 7 (outside agent reach). 2. Hash chaining: each run record includes prev_hash and its own SHA-256; write the daily chain head into Object Lock. Cheap, detects deletion and edit. Matches CNIL para. 12 "timestamp and sign at creation". 3. Signing: sign the daily manifest with a key held in Vault transit (you run Vault) or cosign. Key never visible to agents. 4. Transparency log: Sigstore Rekor v2 is tile-based, needs rekor-tiles plus a timestamp authority, no online inclusion proof API, so it is heavy for a small team. Single-binary Merkle logs such as Etchlog (RFC 6962, single-node) exist, maturity unchecked. Source: Sigstore docs and project READMEs via search. [LOW]. I would skip this for the demo. 5. VictoriaLogs and VictoriaTraces are mutable operational stores. Do not present them as the evidence store. Present them as the query layer, with the Object Lock copy as evidence.

docs.title: B4. Open-source LLM observability tools vs Victoria stack
docs.text:
Stars and push dates from GitHub API 2026-11-13.

Tool Licence Weight (self-host) Adds over Victoria stack Status notes Langfuse MIT core, ee features with license key (GitHub reports NOASSERTION), 37.4k stars Web + worker (docs: at least 2 CPU and 4 GB RAM for all app containers) plus Postgres, ClickHouse, Redis/Valkey, S3. OTLP over HTTP only at /api/public/otel (v3.22.0+), no gRPC; maps gen_ai.* Acquired by ClickHouse 2026-01-16, ClickHouse states MIT core stays. One site claims AGPL, contradicted by official statements. Phoenix (Arize) Elastic License 2.0 per secondary sources, GitHub NOASSERTION, 12.3k stars Not found on pages read Evals, datasets, experiments, OTel/OpenInference tracing Arize independent per Hackernoon 2026-08-27, one site claims a Dynatrace deal, unresolved. Source-available, not OSI. [MED] Opik (Comet) Apache-2.0, 23.4k stars Not found Evals, datasets, online scoring, dashboards Independent. OpenLIT Apache-2.0, 3.1k stars SDK plus optional platform; VM official post shows the pipeline without its UI Auto-instrumentation, cost, evals (server side in platform) Active, officially paired with VM stack. Helicone Apache-2.0, 6.3k stars Not checked Proxy-based logging, caching Acquired by Mintlify 2026-03-03, "maintenance mode". Avoid. Lunary Licence conflicting in sources (Apache-2.0 vs source-available) Not checked Prompt management, evals GitHub API returned 404 for lunary-ai/lunary on 2026-11-13, status unclear. Avoid. Sources: https://langfuse.com/self-hosting , https://langfuse.com/self-hosting/deployment/infrastructure/containers , https://langfuse.com/integrations/native/opentelemetry , https://clickhouse.com/blog/clickhouse-acquires-langfuse-open-source-llm-observability , https://hackernoon.com/two-acquisitions-deep-two-still-standing-whats-really-happening-to-open-source-llm-observability

Recommendation for a RAM-scarce cluster [BEST PRACTICE] - Stay on the Victoria stack plus one OTel Collector. It already gives cost, latency, tool-call audit, guardrail alerts and a join through trace IDs, with no extra datastore. Every tool above brings its own database tier, and the heaviest (Langfuse: ClickHouse + Postgres + Redis + S3) duplicates what you already run. - Add Langfuse only if a concrete need appears: prompt versioning, datasets, human annotation or eval workflows that tenants ask for. Treat it as an optional per-tenant add-on, not a platform dependency. agentgateway has a documented Langfuse integration (blog 2026-02-17), so you can fan out later. - Do not adopt Helicone or Lunary. - Evals: start with a scheduled Go or Python job that replays sampled runs and emits gen_ai.evaluation.result events or a gen_ai_evaluation_score metric.

docs.title: B5. What "impressive and compliant" looks like for the demo
docs.text: One run, one trace, one record: 1. Root span at the CMP/MCP entry: Keycloak user (sub, hashed email), project/tenant, assistant client, requested action, correlation id. Disclosure shown to the user (Art. 50(1) evidence). 2. Child spans: invoke_agent (kagent), chat spans per model call through agentgateway (provider, model, tokens, cost, guardrail verdicts), execute_tool spans per MCP call (tool name, argument hash), sandbox exec span (command hash, exit code, egress policy hits), then the deployment span (Argo CD sync, commit SHA, image digest). 3. Approval events in the same trace: needs_user_confirmation asked, answered by whom, needs_cmp_approval pending, approved by whom in CMP, the exact action hash executed. The Kubernetes, Vault, Keycloak and Argo CD audit logs already exist and join on user and time. Link them by commit SHA, deployment name and Keycloak sub. 4. Grafana "run view" dashboard: trace waterfall, cost, approval timeline, guardrail hits, link to the evidence object. 5. "AI Act record" export per run: a signed JSON (and optional PDF) produced by a small Go tool querying VictoriaTraces and VictoriaLogs by trace_id. Fields: run id, time window, user, project, system and model versions (agent version, gateway version, model name and provider, local model digest), disclosure version, list of model calls with token and cost, list of tool calls with argument hashes, approvals with approver identity, guardrail verdicts, resulting artefacts (commit, image digest, deployment), content references (pointer to opt-in content object or "not captured"), prev_hash and hash. Stored in the Object Lock bucket. Same fields map to Art. 12(2) purposes and the CNIL "demande, autorisation, action, resultat" sequence of ANSSI. 6. Privacy posture to show: content capture off by default, per-project opt-in switch, redaction at the gateway, retention dashboard, a DSAR search by hashed user id. 7. Label it honestly: "built to the Art. 12/19/26(6) shape, not a conformity claim, no harmonised standard yet".

docs.title: B6. Open questions and conflicts
docs.text:
• OTel token metric naming (older gen_ai.client.token.usage vs new gen_ai.client.inference.usage.*) differs between spec main and emitters. Pin versions.
  • Content-capture env var: spec says OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_CONTENT, a secondary source says Python instrumentation still reads OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT. Verify per library.
  • agentgateway: prompt/completion content logging not documented on pages read, guardrail verdict field names, inbound traceparent continuation, per-project metric labels. Check live.
  • kagent 1.0 tracing docs and the exact content-capture switch not found.
  • NIS2 France: outcome of the 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-13 Assemblee session unknown.
  • Art. 50(2) applicability to internal dev agents and Art. 72 plan deadline (2027-09-02) not cross-checked on EUR-Lex.
  • France AI Act authority designation unsettled.
  • EN 18286 OJ date (2026-10-14) from a secondary source. Commission page says it was published as Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2274.
  • prEN ISO/IEC 24970 final status unknown.

docs.title: VictoriaMetrics ecosystem, state of the art as of 2026-11-13
docs.text: Target: small k3s platform, 2 nodes, 28 GB RAM, 8 vCPU, Ceph RBD plus Ceph RGW S3. About 70 pods, up to 200k active series, 5 to 20 GB logs/day. Confidence tags: [HIGH] primary source read in full or in relevant part, [MED] secondary or vendor benchmark, [LOW] inferred or estimate. Data older than 12 months is flagged [STALE]. All GitHub figures below were read from the GitHub API or release pages on 2026-11-13.

docs.title: 0. Executive conclusions
docs.text:
1. Use the operator, installed through victoria-metrics-k8s-stack 0.98.1 (appVersion v1.156.0), with VMSingle, not VMCluster. Your multitenancy is already label based through vmauth extra_filters, so VMCluster brings no isolation gain at this scale. [HIGH]
  2. VictoriaLogs single-node is production ready (GA since v1.0.0, current v1.54.0 released 2026-11-13). It cannot use S3 yet and cannot do per-stream or per-tenant retention. Both are real regressions against your Loki setup. [HIGH]
  3. VictoriaTraces is still pre-GA (v0.13.0, 2026-11-05). Its roadmap says the data structure is not yet frozen. Usable on a tiny cluster, but treat it as beta. [HIGH]
  4. Replace Alloy with vmagent for metrics and vlagent for logs. Zero-code traces and RED metrics: OBI v1.0.0 (stable, 2026-10-30). [HIGH]
  5. Enterprise-only items that matter to you: retention filters, downsampling, vmanomaly, multi-tenant vmalert and VMRule tenant field, vmbackupmanager, vmauth IP filters. Everything else you need is open source. [HIGH]
  6. Realistic RAM for the whole target stack is about 4 to 6 GB, against roughly 1.8 GB for Alloy alone today. See section 8. Most figures are estimates and must be measured. [LOW]

docs.title: 1. Operator vs Helm charts, k8s-stack, VMSingle vs VMCluster, tenancy, OSS vs Enterprise
1.1 Operator status
docs.text:
• Operator latest v0.75.2 (released 28 Oct 2026). v0.75.0 released 25 Sep 2026. Helm chart victoria-metrics-operator 0.68.2 (2026-10-28). Repo 600 stars, Apache-2.0. [HIGH] https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/operator/releases
  • CRDs listed in the docs: VMSingle, VMCluster, VMAgent, VMAlert, VMAlertmanager, VMAlertmanagerConfig, VMAuth, VMUser, VMRule, VMServiceScrape, VMPodScrape, VMNodeScrape, VMStaticScrape, VMScrapeConfig, VMProbe, VMAnomaly, VLSingle, VLCluster, VLAgent, VTSingle, VTCluster, VTAgent, VMDistributed, plus VLDistributed. [HIGH] https://docs.victoriametrics.com/operator/resources/
  • New in 2026: VLDistributed (v0.74.0), VTAgent (v0.75.0). [HIGH]
  • Breaking or update notes to read before upgrading: v0.75.0 config-reloader argument change rolls many pods once. VMCluster vmstorage serviceSpec that makes the Service non-headless is rejected. VTAgent needs extra RBAC or the operator shuts down. v0.74.0 needs NetworkPolicy permissions in the ClusterRole and disables prometheus-operator validation webhooks by default. [HIGH]
  • VMAgent has daemonSetMode since operator v0.55.0, but it supports only VMPodScrape and cannot combine with statefulMode. Not useful for you, a single Deployment replica is enough at 200k series. [HIGH] https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/operator/blob/master/docs/api.md (field daemonSetMode)
  • VMAnomaly CRD (since operator v0.60.0) is Enterprise only: "VMAnomaly is enterprise only, license is required for this CRD". [HIGH] https://docs.victoriametrics.com/operator/resources/vmanomaly/
  • VMAlertmanagerConfig has an enforced namespace matcher: alerts need a namespace label equal to the config's namespace, unless VMAlertmanager spec.disableNamespaceMatcher is true. Useful for per-project routing to Discord. [HIGH] https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/operator/blob/master/docs/resources/vmalertmanagerconfig.md
  • VMRule tenant field is Enterprise only. [HIGH] https://docs.victoriametrics.com/operator/enterprise/

docs.title: 1.2 Operator vs plain charts
docs.text:
• The operator buys you CRD-driven config: VMServiceScrape/VMPodScrape/VMNodeScrape/VMProbe, VMRule per namespace, VMUser per project, VMAlertmanagerConfig per namespace. These match the "project = set of namespaces" model, and prometheus-operator CRDs can be converted automatically (docs list a conversion path). [HIGH]
  • Plain charts (victoria-metrics-single 0.51.0, victoria-metrics-cluster 0.55.0, victoria-metrics-agent 0.52.0, victoria-metrics-alert 0.53.0, victoria-metrics-auth 0.46.0, victoria-logs-single 0.13.12, victoria-traces-single 0.1.13) were all published 2026-11-09. They remain maintained. [HIGH] https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/helm-charts/releases
  • Operator cost: one extra controller pod. Memory not measured. [LOW]
  • Recommendation: operator, because per-project VMUser, VMRule and scrape CRDs are exactly the self-service surface an IDP needs.

docs.title: 1.3 victoria-metrics-k8s-stack 0.98.1 contents (read from Chart.yaml and values.yaml)
docs.text:
• appVersion v1.156.0, kubeVersion >= 1.25. Dependencies: victoria-metrics-operator 0.68., kube-state-metrics 9.0., prometheus-node-exporter 4.60., grafana 14.4. from the grafana-community chart repo. [HIGH] https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VictoriaMetrics/helm-charts/master/charts/victoria-metrics-k8s-stack/Chart.yaml
  • Enabled by default: vmsingle (retention 1 month, 20Gi RWO PVC), vmagent, vmalert, alertmanager, grafana, defaultRules, defaultDashboards via a sync job, scrape of kubelet, kubeApiServer, kubeControllerManager, kubeEtcd, kubeScheduler. Disabled by default: vmcluster, vmauth, vlsingle, vlcluster, vlagent, vtsingle, vtcluster, kubeProxy. [HIGH] https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VictoriaMetrics/helm-charts/master/charts/victoria-metrics-k8s-stack/values.yaml
  • The chart can provision Grafana datasources for VictoriaMetrics (prometheus type and victoriametrics-metrics-datasource), VictoriaLogs (victoriametrics-logs-datasource) and VictoriaTraces (jaeger type). The plugins must be listed in grafana.plugins, and Grafana needs internet access to install them. [HIGH]
  • Caveats for your setup:
  • You run your own Grafana 12.3 with one org per project. The chart's dashboard sidecar provider is bound to orgid 1, so default dashboards land in org 1 only. Disable the bundled grafana and provision dashboards per org yourself. [LOW, inferred from values.yaml provider.orgid: 1]
  • kubeControllerManager, kubeEtcd and kubeScheduler scrapes are on by default. k3s embeds these in one process and does not expose them as separate pods, so expect down targets and noisy default alerts unless you disable them. [LOW, inferred]
  • kube-state-metrics and node-exporter are bundled, you can drop your standalone copies.

docs.title: 1.4 VMSingle vs VMCluster
docs.text:
• Vendor guidance: use single-node below one million data points per second. Single node needs less CPU and RAM than cluster for the same workload, is easier to operate, and supports HA. [HIGH] https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/ and https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/faq/
  • The FAQ lists cluster as preferable mainly for native multitenancy or for workloads beyond what one node handles. It also states multitenancy can be done with labels and vmauth enforced query args on single node. [HIGH]
  • Your load is 200k active series, which is about 0.2 percent of the 100M series single-node scale claim in the docs. [HIGH]
  • Migration cluster to single: data formats differ. The documented path is to run both in parallel until old data ages out, or use vmctl native export/import. The docs describe single to cluster explicitly. Cluster to single is the reverse via vmctl. [MED] https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/faq/
  • Recommendation: VMSingle, one replica, PVC on Ceph RBD, 30 to 90 day retention. Backups with vmbackup to RGW S3 (open source, supports any S3 compatible store including Ceph). [HIGH] https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmbackup/

docs.title: 1.5 Multitenancy options
docs.text:
Option Needs Works on Notes Label filtering with vmauth extra_filters and extra_label vmauth user per project VMSingle and VMCluster Open source. Your current model. Isolation is only as strong as the label provenance, enforce at both write and read. [HIGH] accountID/projectID tenants VMCluster VMCluster only Single node has no multitenancy. Headers AccountID and ProjectID work since v1.143.0, on by default since v1.150.0. [HIGH] vm_account_id and vm_project_id labels with the multitenant endpoints VMCluster VMCluster Lets one writer or reader span tenants. Restrict access to these endpoints. [HIGH] Per-tenant retention, per-tenant stats, per-tenant rate limits Enterprise VMCluster -retentionFilter with vm_account_id, vmgateway. [HIGH]

Sources: https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/ , https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmauth/ - vmauth templating from JWT claims (metrics_extra_filters, metrics_extra_labels, logs_extra_filters, logs_extra_stream_filters) is open source and exists since v1.137.0. OIDC discovery, JWT claim matching and deny_paths are open source. So Grafana per-org datasources can use a JWT or basic-auth user per project. [HIGH] - Project label at write time: vmagent kubernetes_sd supports attach_metadata namespace true, exposing _meta_kubernetes_namespace_label. You can stamp a project label from a namespace label during relabeling. [HIGH] https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/sd_configs/ - Cardinality control: cardinality explorer in vmui, vmagent -remoteWrite.maxHourlySeries and maxDailySeries, per-scrape series_limit and sample_limit, vmstorage or VMSingle -storage.maxHourlySeries and -storage.maxDailySeries. These limits are global. Per-tenant limits are Enterprise (vmgateway). [HIGH for flags, MED for the per-tenant claim] https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmagent/ and https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/enterprise/ - Per-project alert rules with one open source vmalert: groups can carry params with extra_label or extra_filters for the project, or run one vmalert per tenant. The group tenant field and -clusterMode are Enterprise. [HIGH] https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmalert/

docs.title: 1.6 Open source vs Enterprise (VictoriaMetrics)
docs.text: Enterprise only: downsampling, retention filters (multiple retentions), vmbackupmanager, vmanomaly, advanced per-tenant stats, query execution stats, vmgateway, mTLS and auto TLS, vmauth mTLS routing and IP filters, vmalert multitenancy and reading rules from object storage, Kafka and PubSub integration, vmstorage auto discovery, FIPS builds. [HIGH] https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/enterprise/ Open source and relevant: vmbackup and vmrestore to S3, vmctl, stream aggregation and deduplication, vmalert, vmalert-tool, cardinality explorer, vmauth including JWT and OIDC, vmagent cardinality limiter, relabeling debugger. [HIGH] Licensing changes: from v1.156.0 (2026-11-09) Enterprise components take an -eula flag and license keys are no longer verified. Production use still requires an enterprise contract. Evaluation use is allowed non-production. [HIGH] LTS lines are published for Enterprise only. Currently v1.148.x and v1.136.x. Open source users are told to track the latest release. [HIGH] https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/lts-releases/ Implication: you cannot get VM-native per-tenant retention, so give every project the same retention, or run a second VMSingle for long-lived data and route with vmauth.

docs.title: 1.7 Version and bug watchlist
docs.text:
• v1.154.0 carried an OOM risk on long-range series and label queries and connection churn with -search.skipSlowReplicas. Fixed in v1.155.0 and v1.156.0. v1.154.0 also fixed a vmauth token brute-force issue and a vmui XSS. v1.152.0 fixed a vmauth JWT authorization bypass. v1.151.0 fixed an HTTP Basic Auth bypass on suffixed paths. Run at least v1.156.0 when exposing vmauth. [HIGH] https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/releases
  • v1.155.0: /admin/tenants returns only the current day without start and end. v1.150.0: -enableMultitenancyViaHeaders defaults to true. v1.148.1: delete_series is POST only. [HIGH]

docs.title: 2.1 Maturity and versions
docs.text:
• VictoriaLogs repo created 2025-07-06 (split out from the main repo), 2500 stars, Apache-2.0. Latest v1.54.0 (2026-11-13), v1.53.0 (2026-10-01), LTS line v1.52.x (v1.52.2, Enterprise-targeted). [HIGH] https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaLogs/releases
  • FAQ: "Yes. VictoriaLogs is ready for production use starting from v1.0.0." [HIGH] https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victorialogs/faq/
  • Release cadence is fast and includes breaking changes within minor versions. Examples: v1.51.0 rejects filter pipes without the filter prefix, v1.53.0 requires POST on /internal/*, mixed-version cluster queries fail during rolling upgrades in several releases. Pin versions and read the changelog on each bump. [HIGH] https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victorialogs/changelog/

docs.title: 2.2 Single vs cluster
docs.text:
• Docs: use single-node if one host can handle the load. It is simpler and faster on the same hardware. Cluster mode (vlinsert, vlselect, vlstorage, same binary with -storageNode) only for vertical scaling limits. Cluster shards, it does not replicate. [HIGH] https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victorialogs/cluster/
  • At 5 to 20 GB/day, single node. [HIGH on the guidance, LOW on the exact threshold]

docs.title: 2.3 Storage, S3, retention
docs.text:
• Local disk only today. Data lives in per-day partitions under one directory. [HIGH] https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victorialogs/
  • Object storage: still on the roadmap. Issue #48 open. PR #1155 "introduce object storage support" open. On 2026-10-08 valyala wrote the merge ETA is November 2026. Design: per-day partitions older than -offloadPeriod (minimum one day) move to object storage, recent data stays local, moved data remains queryable. [HIGH] https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaLogs/issues/48 Open bug reports on the PR build: on 2026-11-02 a user reported queries on data older than 7 days crash the process on any S3 error and stop ingestion, and an interrupted offload can cause a restart loop until the day folder is removed by hand. On 2026-11-05 the author said an unavailable object store causes the restart loop because startup treats a failed remote listing as fatal. Do not plan on S3 offload before it ships and stabilises. [HIGH, dates as quoted]
  • Backups: snapshots plus rclone to S3 or GCS are documented. Native backup tooling is a roadmap item (issue #123). [HIGH] https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaLogs/master/docs/victorialogs/Roadmap.md
  • Retention: global -retentionPeriod (default 7d) and disk-based -retention.maxDiskSpaceUsageBytes or -retention.maxDiskUsagePercent, mutually exclusive. No per-tenant, per-stream or per-level retention flag exists in the open source flag list or in the Enterprise flag list. [HIGH] https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaLogs/master/docs/victorialogs/victoria_logs_enterprise_flags.md
  • Issue #15 "retentionPeriod for different streams" is closed (last update 2025-12-05). The maintainer position: VM Enterprise retention filters were "a mistake" because of reliability and resource cost. The supported pattern is several independent VictoriaLogs instances with different retentions, fronted by vmauth routing, plus the victoria-logs-multilevel Helm chart (0.2.10 as of 2026-11-02) for querying them together. [HIGH] https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaLogs/issues/15 https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victorialogs/security-and-lb/
  • Consequence for you: your Loki per-stream retention rules must become two or three VLSingle instances (for example 7d, 30d, 90d), with the collector or vmauth deciding the destination. Each extra instance costs RAM. [LOW on cost]

docs.title: 2.4 Multitenancy
docs.text:
• Tenant is (AccountID, ProjectID), 32-bit each, set by request headers on ingest and query. Thousands of tenants per instance is described as fine. VictoriaLogs does no authorization itself, use vmauth. [HIGH]
  • vmauth can force headers per user, route by tenant header, and apply extra_filters and extra_stream_filters query args to restrict access. Both args are documented on the query API. [HIGH] https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaLogs/master/docs/victorialogs/querying/README.md
  • vlagent Kubernetes collector: documented tenant selection is per remoteWrite through -remoteWrite.headers, or the /insert/multitenant/native endpoint for mixed tenants arriving via ingestion protocols. I found no documented per-namespace tenant routing in the Kubernetes collector. Log transformation in vlagent is still a roadmap item (#858). [HIGH for what is documented, LOW for the absence claim]
  • Practical design: ship everything to one tenant and enforce project isolation in vmauth with extra_stream_filters on kubernetes.pod_namespace, which is a default stream field. This mirrors your current extra_filters model for metrics. [MED, design inference from docs]
  • Per-tenant stats and quotas on ingest rate, stream cardinality and query cost are Enterprise roadmap items, not shipped. [HIGH]

docs.title: 2.5 Query language and Grafana
docs.text:
• LogsQL. LogQL conversion guide and playground exist; no migration tool yet (roadmap issue #521). I found no native Loki query API in VictoriaLogs; a third-party Loki-VL-proxy exists but I did not verify it. [HIGH for the guide, LOW for the proxy] https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victorialogs/logql-to-logsql/
  • Grafana plugin victoriametrics-logs-datasource: v0.34.0 (2026-11-06), Apache-2.0, 204 stars, has a Drilldown view. Grafana's Logs Drilldown for Loki does not apply. [HIGH] https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/victorialogs-datasource
  • Rules on logs: vmalert with rule type vlogs, enabled per group or with -rule.defaultRuleType=vlogs. v1.51.0 added limit and offset pipes in stats_query for rules. Rules on logs and metrics need separate vmalert instances or typed groups. [HIGH] https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victorialogs/vmalert/

docs.title: 2.6 Ingestion protocols and collectors
docs.text:
• HTTP endpoints: Elasticsearch bulk /insert/elasticsearch/_bulk, JSON lines /insert/jsonline, Loki push /insert/loki/api/v1/push, OTLP /insert/opentelemetry/v1/logs. Also Syslog, Filebeat, Fluent Bit, Fluentd, Logstash, Vector, Promtail, Alloy, Telegraf, OTel Collector, Journald, Datadog, Splunk (Splunk added v1.50.0). [HIGH] https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victorialogs/data-ingestion/
  • vlagent: log collector with Kubernetes pod log discovery (-kubernetesCollector, DaemonSet), file collector by glob, replication, disk buffering. Deployed by the victoria-logs-collector chart (0.3.8) or the VLAgent CRD. No journald collector in vlagent docs I read, use journald forwarding or Fluent Bit for node journals. [HIGH, journald absence LOW] https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victorialogs/vlagent/
  • vmagent does not collect logs. [HIGH by omission in vmagent docs]

docs.title: 2.7 Benchmarks, all vendor or single-author, treat as directional
docs.text: Source Date Conditions Result VictoriaMetrics docs current not stated "up to 30x less RAM, up to 15x less disk than Elasticsearch and Loki" [MED, vendor claim] TrueFoundry author, dev.to mirror of harshit.cloud post 2025-11-19 4 vCPU 8 GiB nodes, about 500 GB over 7 days, 65 MB/s via flog and Vector, block cache off, versions unstated Loki 6 to 7 GB RAM vs about 1.3 GB, disk 501 GB vs 318 GB, needle query 12 s vs 0.9 s. Internal inconsistencies noted in the post [MED] https://dev.to/sachincool/victorialogs-vs-loki-real-world-benchmarking-results-26bg - Your volume is far below those test loads, so absolute numbers will not transfer. The FAQ advises ingesting 1 to 10 percent of production logs and measuring. [HIGH]

docs.title: 2.8 Migration path from Loki
docs.text:
1. Deploy VLSingle (or several, see 2.3) and a vlagent DaemonSet. Dual-ship during the longest retention window, or point Alloy loki.write at the VictoriaLogs Loki endpoint for a quick start.
  2. Rewrite dashboards and alerts from LogQL to LogsQL, Loki ruler rules to vmalert vlogs groups.
  3. Keep Loki read-only until its retention expires, then remove it and its RGW bucket.
  4. Disk: logs compress about 10x or more per the docs, so 5 to 20 GB/day raw is roughly 0.5 to 2 GB/day on disk. 30 days is about 15 to 60 GB on RBD. [MED] Steps are my synthesis of the cited docs. [LOW]

docs.title: 3. VictoriaTraces
docs.text:
• v0.13.0 (2026-11-05). Repo 521 stars, Apache-2.0, created 2025-07-07. Releases are 0.x. Roadmap states GA requires "Finalize the data structure and commit to backward compatibility". [HIGH] https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaTraces/master/docs/victoriatraces/roadmap.md
  • Breaking behaviours already seen: v0.9.4 changed the internal vtselect/vtstorage protocol so mixed versions fail, v0.12.0 replaced the UI and required POST on some internal endpoints. [HIGH]
  • Ingestion: OTLP over HTTP at /insert/opentelemetry/v1/traces and OTLP/gRPC. vtagent exists (operator CRD VTAgent). Multitenancy through AccountID and ProjectID headers, auth via vmauth. [HIGH] https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriatraces/data-ingestion/
  • Query: Jaeger Query Service JSON API, Tempo HTTP API marked experimental, TraceQL fuzzy and regex matching appears in the v0.9.1 release notes. Grafana uses the Jaeger datasource. [HIGH]
  • Service graph: /select/jaeger/api/dependencies is experimental and needs -servicegraph.enableTask=true. [HIGH] https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaTraces/master/docs/victoriatraces/querying/README.md
  • RED metrics derived from traces: not found in the VictoriaTraces docs. Use OBI span_metrics and service_graph_metrics, or the OTel Collector spanmetrics connector, and send the result to vmagent. [LOW on absence, HIGH that OBI offers it, see section 5]
  • Storage: local disk only, retention global (-retentionPeriod default 7d), no S3, same per-day partition design as VictoriaLogs. [HIGH]
  • Alerting through vmalert. [HIGH]
  • Benchmark [STALE - 2025-06-09], vendor, proof of concept predating VictoriaTraces: at 10k spans/s with 4 CPU and 8 GiB, VictoriaLogs-based tracing used 0.50 vCPU and 1.15 GiB, ClickHouse 0.69 vCPU and 1.12 GiB, Tempo 1.35 vCPU and 4.26 GiB and ran out of memory. Jaeger plus Elasticsearch was unstable above about 5,000 spans/s. Versions not stated. [MED] https://victoriametrics.com/blog/dev-note-distributed-tracing-with-victorialogs/

Comparison for a tiny cluster | | VictoriaTraces 0.13 | Tempo 3.1.1 (2026-10-21) | Jaeger 2.23.0 (2026-11-05) | |---|---|---|---| | Maturity | pre-GA | GA, AGPL-3.0 | GA, Apache-2.0 | | Storage | local disk | object storage, fits your RGW | Badger (dev scale), Elasticsearch, Cassandra, ClickHouse experimental per one third-party source [LOW] | | Footprint | lowest in vendor test | monolithic mode, no Kafka needed in 3.0 | collector plus query plus a store | | Query | Jaeger API, Tempo API experimental | TraceQL, TraceQL metrics GA in 3.0 | Jaeger UI | | Multitenancy | headers via vmauth | native tenant header | limited | Tempo 3.0 microservices mode requires a Kafka-compatible system, monolithic mode does not. [HIGH] https://grafana.com/docs/tempo/latest/release-notes/v3-0/ Recommendation: VictoriaTraces if you accept pre-GA and want one vendor stack. Tempo monolithic if you need frozen formats and TraceQL metrics. [LOW, judgement]

docs.title: 4.1 Benchmarks
docs.text:
• Log collectors, VictoriaMetrics benchmark dated 2026-03-20, GCP n2-highcpu-32 single-node kind, about 10k logs/s at 216 bytes, 1 CPU and 1 GiB limits, default Helm values. vlagent v1.48.0, Vector v0.53.0, Alloy v1.13.2, Fluent Bit v4.2.3, OTel Collector v0.146.1. [MED, vendor] https://victoriametrics.com/blog/log-collectors-benchmark-2026/ | Collector | CPU cores | Mean memory MiB | |---|---|---| | vlagent | 0.062 | 27.9 | | Fluent Bit | 0.260 | 78.1 | | Vector | 0.412 | 153.5 | | OTel Collector | 0.491 | 106.8 | | Grafana Alloy | 0.578 | 66.4 | Filebeat and Fluentd dropped logs and were excluded.
  • Metrics agents, VictoriaMetrics post [STALE - 2025-02-05]: scraping 1,200 node exporters on 2 vCPU 2 GB instances. vmagent v1.108.0 used 3.2x less CPU and 2.7x less memory than OTel Collector v0.115.0, 1.6x less CPU and 3.0x less memory than Prometheus 3.x agent mode. Alloy not tested. Figures only in charts. [MED] https://victoriametrics.com/blog/opentelemetry-prometheus-and-more/
  • Alloy official sizing: about 0.4 CPU and 11 GiB RAM per 1M active series, and about 1 CPU and 120 MiB per 1 MiB/s of logs. Applies to its Prometheus pipeline, which keeps a WAL. This explains why a DaemonSet that both scrapes metrics and tails logs reaches 900 MB per node. [MED] https://grafana.com/docs/alloy/latest/set-up/estimate-resource-usage/ A community report of 742 MiB growing over days exists but has no confirmed fix. [LOW]

docs.title: 4.2 Best combination for this platform
docs.text: Signal Collector Reason Metrics vmagent as one VMAgent Deployment Lowest footprint in vendor tests, native relabeling, stream aggregation, series limits, kubernetes_sd namespace metadata. DaemonSet mode only supports VMPodScrape so avoid it. Logs vlagent DaemonSet (victoria-logs-collector chart 0.3.8) 28 MiB and 0.06 CPU at 10k logs/s in vendor test, native Kubernetes metadata, checkpoint file, disk buffer. Traces from SDKs OTLP direct to VictoriaTraces OTel Operator Instrumentation CRD injects the SDK and points it at VT. Traces and RED without code change OBI DaemonSet See section 5. Gateway OTel Collector only if you need tail sampling, spanmetrics connector, or attribute processing Otherwise skip, it costs roughly 100 MiB or more. - Fluent Bit is the fallback for node journald or per-namespace tenant routing, at about 78 MiB in the same test. Vector at 154 MiB is the heaviest of the viable options. [MED] - OTel Operator v0.163.0 (2026-11-11). Auto-instrumentation supports Apache HTTPD, DotNet, Go, Java, Nginx, NodeJS, PHP, Python, Ruby. The Instrumentation CRD is still apiVersion opentelemetry.io/v1alpha1. Injection is by pod or namespace annotation. [HIGH] https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-operator/blob/main/docs/auto-instrumentation/README.md - vmagent accepts OTLP metrics at /opentelemetry/v1/metrics. VictoriaLogs and VictoriaTraces accept OTLP natively, so no vendor-specific exporter is required. [HIGH] - Stream aggregation, deduplication and relabeling are open source in vmagent and VMSingle. [HIGH] https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/stream-aggregation/

docs.title: 5. eBPF zero-code instrumentation
docs.text:
Tool Status 2026-11-13 Outputs Fit OpenTelemetry eBPF Instrumentation (OBI) v1.0.0 stable 2026-10-30. Repo 639 stars, Apache-2.0 [HIGH] OTLP traces, RED metrics, runtime metrics, network flow metrics, span metrics, service graph metrics, built-in Prometheus endpoint Best fit Grafana Beyla v3.41.0 2026-11-04, v3.42.0 pre-release, 2153 stars [HIGH] Same family, Grafana distribution Redundant with OBI Coroot v1.29.2 2026-11-04, 8018 stars [HIGH] Own UI, service map, SLOs, profiling Needs ClickHouse plus a Prometheus-compatible store. Supports VictoriaMetrics as a drop-in. Too many moving parts for 2 nodes [HIGH on requirements, LOW on cost] Pixie CNCF sandbox, Vizier pre-releases only in 2026 [HIGH] Own UI Docs minimum 1 GiB per node, no more than 25 percent of node RAM. Rule out [HIGH] Odigos Not verified. GitHub API returned 404 for odigos-io/odigos. A third-party page lists v1.31.1 from July 2026 [LOW] OTel format Not assessed Cilium Hubble L7 Cilium v1.20.4 stable [HIGH] http_requests_total, http_request_duration_seconds, dns, flow, tcp, drop L7 metrics only for pods with L7 protocol visibility, disabled by default. No traces. Complement, not substitute [HIGH]

OBI details - Requirements: Linux 5.8 or newer, BTF, amd64 or arm64, root or specific capabilities. Validated kernels include 5.15, 6.1, 6.6, 6.12, 6.18. [HIGH] https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-ebpf-instrumentation/blob/v1.0.0/SUPPORT_MATRIX.md - Languages: Java, .NET, Go, Python, Ruby, Node.js, C, C++, Rust. Protocols include HTTP/S, gRPC, Kafka, PostgreSQL, MySQL, Redis, MongoDB. [HIGH] https://opentelemetry.io/docs/zero-code/obi/ - RED metric names in Prometheus form: http_server_request_duration_seconds, http_client_request_duration_seconds. Span metrics and service graph metrics are enabled through the features option. [HIGH, exact feature keys not confirmed] https://opentelemetry.io/docs/zero-code/obi/metrics/ - Known v1.0.0 limitations: application metrics can go missing after pod restart until OBI restarts, child spans can start before parents, port-based discovery can pick a helper process, service graph needs the instance label preserved across multiple OBI instances. [HIGH] https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-ebpf-instrumentation/releases/tag/v1.0.0 - Resource cost: no official numbers. Blog figures range from 40 to 80 MB per node to a 512 MiB limit and are unsourced. Measure on your nodes. [LOW] - Interaction with Cilium eBPF programs: not researched. Test on one node first. [LOW] - Output to the VM stack: OTLP traces to VictoriaTraces, Prometheus endpoint scraped by a VMPodScrape. No collector needed. [MED, design inference]

docs.title: 6. Continuous profiling
docs.text: Option Status Cost and fit Grafana Pyroscope v2.4.3 (2026-11-03), 11.7k stars, AGPL-3.0 [HIGH] Single-binary mode with local filesystem exists but docs say not recommended for production and has no HA. Distributed mode requires object storage. No official small-cluster sizing found. Alloy pyroscope.ebpf figures not found. Parca v0.30.0 (2026-11-06), 5017 stars, Apache-2.0 [HIGH] Polar Signals was acquired by Dash0 on 2026-08-17. Both companies say Parca stays open source and maintained. Direction risk. Sizing not found. OTel profiling signal Public alpha since March 2026, not stable in OTLP, no production backends [HIGH] Do not build on it yet Coroot Built-in profiling Needs the full Coroot stack VictoriaMetrics No profile store exists [HIGH by absence] Not applicable Sources: https://grafana.com/docs/pyroscope/latest/reference-pyroscope-v2-architecture/deployment-modes/ , https://opentelemetry.io/blog/2026/profiles-alpha , https://blog.polarsignals.com/blog/posts/2026/08/17/polar-signals-is-joining-dash0 Recommendation: defer profiling. If wanted later, a single Pyroscope or Parca pod with its own PVC, accept no HA. [LOW]

docs.title: 7. VictoriaMetrics-native tooling
docs.text:
• SLOs: no native SLO engine found. Generate Prometheus-format rules with Sloth (v0.16.0, 2026-04-04) or Pyrra (v0.10.2, 2026-09-18) and wrap them in VMRule. A Pyrra pull request for VictoriaMetrics support from June 2025 exists, merge status not confirmed. [LOW] https://github.com/pyrra-dev/pyrra/pull/1472
  • vmalert-tool unittest: open source, Prometheus-compatible test format except the field name metricsql_expr_test replacing promql_expr_test. Starts an isolated VictoriaMetrics instance. Fits CI for VMRule. [HIGH] https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmalert-tool/
  • Anomaly detection: vmanomaly is Enterprise only and needs a license. Chart victoria-metrics-anomaly 1.12.21. Open source alternatives: MetricsQL zscore, outliers_mad, outliersk, mad plus vmalert. [HIGH] https://docs.victoriametrics.com/anomaly-detection/
  • Grafana plugins: victoriametrics-metrics-datasource v1.0.0 (2026-11-02, AGPL-3.0 licence per GitHub API) and victoriametrics-logs-datasource v0.34.0 (Apache-2.0). The metrics plugin is optional since the Prometheus datasource type works, but the plugin gives MetricsQL support and the Drilldown. Check the AGPL licence against your distribution policy. [HIGH]
  • Perses has VictoriaLogs and VictoriaMetrics datasource integrations if you ever leave Grafana. [MED] https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victorialogs/integrations/perses/
  • MCP servers, all Apache-2.0: mcp-victoriametrics v1.21.0 (2026-11-12, 245 stars), mcp-victorialogs v1.9.0 (2026-04-10, 111 stars), mcp-victoriatraces v1.5.0 (2025-12-15, 19 stars). The metrics server exposes read-only APIs, supports stdio, SSE and streamable HTTP, a Helm chart, VM_DEFAULT_TENANT_ID, and header passthrough via MCP_PASSTHROUGH_HEADERS so you can put it behind vmauth per project. [HIGH] https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/mcp-victoriametrics
  • OpenCost works against VictoriaMetrics: blog guidance sets prometheus.external to the vmselect or vmsingle URL, based on a feature in OpenCost v1.110.0. Current OpenCost v1.121.4 (2026-11-10). No dedicated OpenCost reference page found. [MED] https://opencost.io/blog/victoria-metrics

docs.title: 8. RAM and CPU budget
docs.text:
Assumptions: 2 nodes, about 70 pods, 200k active series at peak, 10 GB/day logs at the middle of your range, a few dozen spans per second. Only rows marked with a source have a published anchor. Everything else is my estimate and must be measured with vmagent and process metrics before sizing requests. All [LOW] unless stated. Requests are what I would start with, limits are where OOM becomes acceptable.

Component Replicas Request RAM Limit RAM CPU request Basis VM operator 1 64 Mi 256 Mi 20m Estimate VMSingle 1 768 Mi 1.5 Gi 300m Docs: under 1 KB per active series, keep 50 percent RAM free. 200k series is about 200 MB resident plus caches and queries. [MED anchor] VMAgent 1 256 Mi 768 Mi 100m Estimate. Vendor says it uses less than Prometheus agent, no absolute number. Alloy rule of 11 GiB per 1M series does not apply to vmagent. vmalert 1 or 2 64 Mi 256 Mi 20m Estimate Alertmanager or VMAlertmanager 1 48 Mi 128 Mi 10m Estimate vmauth 1 48 Mi 128 Mi 20m Estimate kube-state-metrics 1 96 Mi 256 Mi 20m Estimate node-exporter 2 24 Mi 64 Mi 10m Estimate OpenCost 1 96 Mi 256 Mi 20m Estimate VictoriaLogs single 1 512 Mi 1.5 Gi 250m Vendor test shows 1.3 GB at 65 MB/s, you ingest about 0.1 MB/s on average. Heavy queries are the risk. [MED anchor] Extra VLSingle for long retention 1 or 2 256 Mi 768 Mi 100m Needed if you keep per-class retention. Estimate vlagent 2 48 Mi 128 Mi 25m Vendor test: 28 MiB and 0.062 CPU at 10k logs/s. Yours is lower per node. [MED anchor] VictoriaTraces single 1 256 Mi 768 Mi 100m Vendor PoC: 1.15 GiB at 10k spans/s, you send a small fraction. [STALE anchor] OBI DaemonSet 2 128 Mi 384 Mi 50m Unverified blog range 40 to 512 MiB Grafana 12.3 1 256 Mi 512 Mi 100m Existing OTel Collector gateway, optional 1 128 Mi 256 Mi 50m Vendor test 107 MiB at 10k logs/s Pyroscope or Parca, optional 1 512 Mi 1 Gi 100m No official sizing found

Totals, sum of requests - Core without optional rows: about 3.2 GiB requested, about 8 GiB of limits. [LOW] - With optional rows: about 4.0 GiB requested. [LOW] - Today: Alloy alone is about 1.8 GB across two nodes (900 MB each, your figure), plus VMCluster with three components, Loki SingleBinary, and standalone Alertmanager. [HIGH for Alloy, from your report] - Expected saving: Alloy replaced by vmagent plus vlagent plus OBI is roughly 1.5 GB lower on the collection side, and VMCluster to VMSingle removes two components. Net saving of 2 to 4 GB is plausible but unmeasured. [LOW]

Disk, at 200k series and 10 GB/day logs - Metrics: VM compresses to roughly a byte or two per sample. At 200k series and a 30s scrape interval that is about 576M samples per day, so about 0.6 to 1.2 GB/day, 20 to 40 GB for 30 days before dedup. [LOW, estimate] - Logs: about 0.5 to 2 GB/day on disk at 10x or better compression, 15 to 60 GB at 30 days. [MED, docs compression claim] - Traces: small at your span rate. [LOW] - All on Ceph RBD PVCs. VictoriaLogs and VictoriaTraces cannot use RGW until the object storage PR lands. [HIGH] - Docs advise keeping 20 percent disk free and 50 percent spare RAM and CPU for VictoriaMetrics. On 28 GB total you have room, but the limits column above should not all be reached together.

docs.title: 9. Recommended stack
docs.text:
1. victoria-metrics-k8s-stack 0.98.x with operator, VMSingle, VMAgent, VMAlert, VMAlertmanager or your existing Alertmanager, VMAuth. Bundled Grafana off, bundled KSM and node-exporter on.
  2. VLSingle plus VLAgent (or the victoria-logs-collector chart). Add a second VLSingle only for the retention classes you cannot drop.
  3. VTSingle plus OTLP from SDKs and OBI. Accept pre-GA or fall back to Tempo monolithic.
  4. vmauth per project: metrics_extra_filters on the project label, logs extra_stream_filters on pod namespace, trace access by tenant header.
  5. vmalert-tool unit tests in CI for VMRule. Sloth or Pyrra output wrapped in VMRule for SLOs.
  6. Hubble stays for network flows and DNS. Enable L7 only on selected pods.
  7. Skip: VMCluster, vmanomaly, Coroot, Pixie, profiling, until a concrete need shows up.

docs.title: 10. Open questions and gaps
docs.text:
• No official RAM figures for vmagent at 200k series, VictoriaTraces, OBI or Pyroscope. Measure.
  • Per-namespace tenant routing in vlagent not documented. Confirm by test or accept the single-tenant plus vmauth filter design.
  • Whether OBI coexists cleanly with Cilium eBPF on your kernel, not researched.
  • Odigos status not verified.
  • Whether the k8s-stack default dashboards can be provisioned into several Grafana orgs without custom work, not verified.
  • VictoriaLogs S3 offload release date, only a stated ETA of November 2026 with open bug reports.
  • Alloy and Loki sizing on your cluster come from your own report, not measured here.

docs.title: Runbook · Budget d'erreur qui brûle (SLO)
docs.text: Votre app consomme son budget d'erreur plus vite que prévu. Le message Discord dit à quel rythme et combien de temps il reste avant d'épuiser le budget de la période.

docs.title: Ce que l'alerte veut dire
docs.text:
Chaque app de prod a deux objectifs par défaut : 99,5 % de requêtes sans erreur 5xx et 95 % des requêtes servies en moins de 500 ms, sur 7 jours (projets de démo) ou 28 jours. Le CMP génère trois alertes par objectif :

Alerte Rythme Fenêtres Sévérité Budget épuisé en Brûlure rapide 14,4 fois 1 h et 5 min critical environ 2 jours sur 28 Brûlure moyenne 6 fois 6 h et 30 min critical environ 5 jours sur 28 Brûlure lente 1 fois 3 jours et 6 h warning la fin de la période

L'alerte ne sonne pas sous 60 requêtes par heure ni pendant que l'app dort (offhours-guard).

docs.title: Vérifier
docs.text:
1. Ouvrez le lien Portail du message : l'onglet Overview montre le taux d'erreur, la latence et le budget restant, avec les déploiements en marqueurs.
  2. Un déploiement juste avant le début ? Comparez canary et stable dans l'onglet Releases.
  3. Onglet Logs : les erreurs les plus fréquentes de la dernière heure, groupées par motif. Cliquez une ligne pour ouvrir sa trace.
  4. Une dépendance lente (base, autre app) ? L'onglet Traces montre où part le temps.

docs.title: Agir
docs.text:
• Version fautive : revenez à la version précédente depuis Releases. Si le canary tournait, il a peut-être déjà avorté de lui-même.
  • Charge inhabituelle : vérifiez les limites mémoire et CPU dans Settings, et les redémarrages dans Overview.
  • Dépendance : prévenez son équipe ; l'alerte reste ouverte tant que le taux ne redescend pas.
  • Objectif trop strict pour cette app : l'owner le règle dans Settings, onglet SLO.

docs.title: Mettre en sourdine
docs.text: Le lien Sourdine du message ouvre le portail. La sourdine ne vaut que pour votre projet et dure au plus 7 jours. Elle n'arrête pas la brûlure du budget : elle évite seulement de répéter le message pendant que vous corrigez.
